pr.title: Draw the band as one panel on a background that follows the theme
pr.head: 42f2c735da92b297341b8b52a9b081081ba637b1

summary: Projector's band is the strip a Claude Code plugin draws above the prompt. It lists the session's tracked pull requests and the inbox's questions and notices, one line each. In a terminal, it used to draw those rows straight onto the transcript's background, under a ─ divider that held the counts and the time since the last reload. When the band scrolled, you could not easily tell which lines were the band's.

This change draws the band, in a terminal only, as one panel with a background of its own. The panel is inset one column from the terminal's edge, padded one column at each side and one row at its bottom, and it ends at bodyColumns, the column where Claude Code draws the band's [-] collapse mark. A header replaces the divider: /projector at its left, and the counts and the reload's age at its right, all in the theme's subtle color.

The background follows the Claude Code theme, a step darker than the terminal so the panel reads as sunken. A new panel.background setting in .projector.toml overrides it. Claude Desktop, VS Code, and the mobile app draw as before, with no panel and no header.

groups.title: A setting for the panel's color
groups.kicker: The CLI learns the panel.background key, so config set and unset change it.
intro: project config reads and writes Projector's settings in .projector.toml files, layered from the repository out to ~/.projector.toml. It only sets keys listed in SETTINGS. This group adds panel.background as a string, so you can set it with project config set panel.background 'rgb(30,30,40)' --user, and documents it in the settings table.

files.note: Sets, reads, and unsets the key the way the band reads it, with --default auto --json.
Adds the key to the settings table.

groups.title: The band draws as one panel
groups.kicker: register.tsx picks the panel's color and wraps every layout of the band in it.
intro: The band is drawn by a ui.render handler for Claude Code's AbovePrompt component in hooks/register.tsx. It has three layouts: the list of pull requests and items, an open item's drawer, which has the band to itself, and the empty band with its tagline. This group wraps all three in one panel() helper that, in a terminal, nests the lines in an inset Box and a padded Box with a backgroundColor.

The color is kept in two state atoms so the render never waits on a read. bandThemeBackground holds the theme's color, written at session start from $.config.list() and again on each config.set of theme. bandBackground holds the setting, read with project config get once just after start and on every reload. The render uses the setting unless it is auto.

Claude Code refuses a plugin's whole render tree over a color it will not accept, which would make the band disappear. So readBackground checks the setting against PAINTABLE, a pattern of at most 40 letters, digits, and #(),.%_ -, and falls back to auto with one toast for a value that fails it.

checks.text: In a throwaway test under Claude Code 2.1.299's test engine, a Box background was refused for exactly the values PAINTABLE rejects that were tried (ansi:black, the empty string, 41 characters), and accepted for about 20 odd values it passes, such as rgb(1, 2, 3), %, and a 40-character name.

files.note: Adds the panel constants, the theme lookup, the setting read, the theme hooks, and the panel() and header code in the render.

checks.text: The pattern mirrors what the engine refuses, not what it can paint. A name the engine accepts but does not know, such as a misspelled theme key, passes here; the review asked whether a real terminal then draws no background.
A custom theme's slug comes from Claude Code's own theme setting, and the file read stays under the Claude config directory; an unreadable file gives inverseText.
This adds one project config get process to every reload: every 30 seconds while the band is shown, and at the end of each turn.

Traced: the inset Box is bodyColumns wide with one column of left padding, and the panel is columns + 2 wide, so it ends at bodyColumns. The header gap and the open item's rule are the only widths the band works out, and both use columns.

files.note: Declares the two new state atoms, bandThemeBackground and bandBackground.
Pins the panel's shape, the header, the color for each theme and custom theme, a theme change, the setting as written, and the fallback toasts; updates every divider assertion to the header.

intro: docs/plugins.md describes the band for users. It now explains the panel, the color per theme, the header, and a new section on choosing the panel's color, with its examples redrawn. The inbox plan, already completed, gains § 20, which records what changed, why the owner chose a sunken, theme-picked background over inverseText and fixed greys, and which test pins each behavior.
